simulations.title: Gargantua: Relativistic Orbit
simulations.description: Explore how a black hole bends light, changes the orbit of a nearby spacecraft, and slows its clock compared with a distant observer.
simulations.explanation: This model combines gravitational time dilation, orbital motion, and light bending around a non-rotating black hole. Interstellar's Gargantua is rotating, so this simplified Schwarzschild model captures the broad effects rather than the film's full Kerr black-hole geometry.

simulations.title: Earth–Moon Free Return
simulations.description: Adjust a translunar burn and the Moon's position to explore a spacecraft's free-return trajectory, flyby, capture, or impact.
simulations.explanation: A free-return trajectory uses the combined gravity of Earth and the Moon to bring a spacecraft back toward Earth after a lunar flyby. The simulation also models a finite engine burn and the rocket equation, echoing Apollo 13's improvised return path.

simulations.title: Ramp Jump: Vehicle Dynamics
simulations.description: Power a car down a run-up, climb a ramp, and try to land across a gap while air drag, wind, and landing forces affect the outcome.
simulations.explanation: The car accelerates against aerodynamic drag and rolling resistance before leaving a ramp. Its flight follows projectile motion with additional drag; the landing height and impact load determine whether the jump is survivable.

simulations.title: Ripple Interference
simulations.description: Create ripples from two footsteps and watch the waves reinforce or cancel as they cross the water in Jurassic Park's trembling-cup moment.
simulations.explanation: When two waves overlap, their displacements add. In-phase waves make larger ripples (constructive interference); out-of-phase waves reduce one another (destructive interference). Click or drag on the water to add a disturbance.

simulations.title: Magnetic Bottle
simulations.description: Follow charged particles spiraling along magnetic field lines and bouncing between stronger-field ends of a magnetic mirror.
simulations.explanation: A magnetic mirror can confine charged particles when their motion has enough energy perpendicular to the field. Particles inside the loss cone can escape through the ends. The arc-reactor imagery is fictional; magnetic confinement itself is used in real plasma research.

simulations.title: Electric Field Lines
simulations.description: Change the signs and spacing of two charges to see how electric field lines show the direction and strength of their interaction.
simulations.explanation: Electric field lines point away from positive charges and toward negative charges. Their spacing indicates relative field strength. Like charges repel and opposite charges attract; the lines are a visual map of the field, not physical threads.

simulations.title: The Square–Cube Law
simulations.description: Change an organism's height to compare how its supporting strength scales with area while its weight scales with volume.
simulations.explanation: If an object is scaled uniformly, its cross-sectional area grows with the square of its length while its volume and mass grow with the cube. This changes the ratio of supporting strength to weight and is one reason tiny creatures cannot simply be enlarged without biological redesign.

simulations.title: Doppler Effect & Sonic Boom
simulations.description: Watch sound waves bunch up around a moving aircraft and form a Mach cone as its speed reaches and exceeds the speed of sound.
simulations.explanation: A moving sound source changes the spacing of wavefronts for observers ahead of and behind it, producing the Doppler shift. At supersonic speed, overlapping wavefronts form a shock cone; the pressure change is heard as a sonic boom.

simulations.title: Artificial Gravity
simulations.description: Set the radius and rotation rate of a spinning station and see the centripetal acceleration felt by its crew.
simulations.explanation: A rotating habitat can press occupants against its outer rim, creating a sensation similar to gravity. The acceleration depends on both the station's radius and angular speed. 2001: A Space Odyssey uses this idea in its rotating spacecraft interiors.

simulations.title: Buoyancy & Sinking
simulations.description: Change a ship's average density to explore how flooding affects buoyancy and how much of a hull sits below the waterline.
simulations.explanation: A floating body displaces enough water for the buoyant force to balance its weight. If flooding raises the ship's average density above the surrounding water, the hull can no longer displace enough water to stay afloat.

simulations.title: Asteroid Impact Energy
simulations.description: Adjust an asteroid's diameter and speed to compare its impact energy with familiar explosive yields and planetary-scale impacts.
simulations.explanation: Impact energy rises with the square of speed. For an object of fixed density, mass rises with the cube of its diameter, so even a modest increase in asteroid size can sharply raise the energy released at impact.

simulations.title: Electron Interference
simulations.description: Send electrons through multiple slits and observe how de Broglie wavelength, slit spacing, and which-path measurement affect the fringe pattern.
simulations.explanation: Electrons have a de Broglie wavelength and can produce interference patterns after passing through slits. Which-path information changes the observed pattern. This is a visualization of quantum probabilities; it does not mean the electron is a tiny classical wave.

simulations.title: Reactor Criticality
simulations.description: Adjust fuel, moderator, control rods, and cooling to explore a simplified nuclear chain reaction and feedback effects.
simulations.formula: kₑff = neutrons in one generation / previous generation
simulations.explanation: A reactor is critical when each fission generation sustains the next at a steady rate. Moderation can make neutrons more likely to cause fission, control rods absorb neutrons, and fuel temperature and coolant affect the system. This is an educational qualitative model, not an engineering reactor simulator.

simulations.title: Web Swinging
simulations.description: Change the web length and stiffness to see how gravity, elastic tension, and air drag shape a swinging arc. Click the canvas to attach a new web.
simulations.explanation: A web-swing can be approximated as a pendulum, with an elastic tether adding spring force. Gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy during the swing, while air drag steadily removes mechanical energy. The simulation lets you click and drag to attach a web at a new point.

simulations.title: Heat Diffusion
simulations.description: Paint hot and cold patches to watch heat flow across a surface and compare gradual diffusion with the film's dramatic flash-freeze imagery.
simulations.explanation: Heat diffuses from warmer regions toward cooler ones. The heat equation describes how temperature changes over time based on the local temperature gradient. The Day After Tomorrow dramatizes the speed and scale of atmospheric cooling well beyond what real heat diffusion would allow.
